title: Jacob’s prophecy
summary: Jacob addresses his brethren, recalls Zenos’s comparison of the house of Israel to a tame olive-tree, and prophesies that the Lord’s servants shall nourish and prune the vineyard a last time before the end soon comes.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob addresses his brethren and says Zenos likened the house of Israel to a tame olive-tree.
Jacob prophesies that the servants of the Lord shall go forth to nourish and prune his vineyard for the last time, after which the end soon comes.

unspecified_visual_details: Jacob’s appearance, his listeners’ appearance, and the physical setting are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: And now, behold, my brethren, as I said unto you that I would prophesy, behold, this is my prophecy—that the things which this prophet Zenos spake, concerning the house of Israel, in the which he likened them unto a tame olive-tree, must surely come to pass.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

spoken_dialogue.text: and after that the end soon cometh.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The olive-tree and vineyard language belongs to the prophecy; it is not narrated as a visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal olive-tree, vineyard, or servants pruning as a present event.
Do not depict Zenos as physically present.

title: Mercy and warning
summary: Jacob teaches that those who have labored diligently in the vineyard are blessed, warns of being cast out and of the world's future burning, and declares God's mercy toward the house of Israel.

explicit_facts.text: Those who have labored diligently in his vineyard are called blessed; those cast out into their own place are called cursed. The world is said to face fire.
God remembers the house of Israel, both roots and branches, and stretches forth his hands unto them all the day long. Those who do not harden their hearts shall be saved in the kingdom of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob may be shown delivering the teaching.
unspecified_visual_details: Jacob's appearance, audience, and setting are unspecified.

narration.text: And how blessed are they who have labored diligently in his vineyard;
And the world shall be burned with fire.
And how merciful is our God unto us, for he remembereth the house of Israel, both roots and branches;
but as many as will not harden their hearts shall be saved in the kingdom of God.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The warnings and promises are teachings, not events shown taking place.
God's outstretched hands do not establish a visible divine appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal world-wide fire, people being cast out, or a visible divine figure.
Do not invent an audience, location, or details of Jacob's appearance.

title: A plea to repent
summary: Jacob beseeches his brethren to repent, cleave to God, and not harden their hearts.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob beseeches his brethren to repent and cleave unto God.
Jacob urges his hearers not to harden their hearts and asks why they will die.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob addresses a group of brethren.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, clothing, and gestures are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Yea, today, if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts; for why will ye die?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

narration.text: I beseech of you in words of soberness

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The extended arm of mercy is figurative language.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal divine arm or an audible divine voice.

title: Questions about rejecting the word
summary: Jacob asks whether those nourished by the good word of God will bring forth evil fruit and whether his hearers will reject words spoken concerning Christ.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob asks whether those nourished by the good word of God will bring forth evil fruit and be hewn down and cast into the fire.
Jacob asks whether his hearers will reject these words, the words of the prophets, and words spoken concerning Christ.
Jacob asks whether they will deny the good word of Christ, the power of God, and the gift of the Holy Ghost; quench the Holy Spirit; and mock the plan of redemption.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob may be shown addressing hearers.
unspecified_visual_details: Jacob’s appearance, the hearers’ appearance, and the setting are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: For behold, after ye have been nourished by the good word of God all the day long, will ye bring forth evil fruit, that ye must be hewn down and cast into the fire?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, will ye reject these words? Will ye reject the words of the prophets;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Fruit, hewing down, and fire are warning imagery, not narrated physical events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal fruit, cutting, or fire as occurring.
Do not invent a setting or appearances for Jacob or the hearers.

title: The warning of judgment
summary: A warning says that those who do these things will stand with shame and awful guilt before the bar of God and must go into a lake of fire and brimstone described as endless torment.

explicit_facts.text: If the addressed people do these things, the power of redemption and resurrection in Christ will bring them to stand with shame and awful guilt before the bar of God.
The warning says that, according to justice, they must go into a lake of fire and brimstone described as endless torment.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The judgment is being described in a warning, not narrated as a present event.
unspecified_visual_details: No speaker, setting, divine appearance, or visible judgment is described.

narration.text: to stand with shame and awful guilt before the bar of God?
and whose smoke ascendeth up forever and ever, which lake of fire and brimstone is endless torment.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Keep the warned-of judgment distinct from events occurring in the scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict God, condemned people at judgment, or a literal lake as presently visible.
Do not identify or depict an unstated speaker.

title: The strait gate
summary: Jacob urges his brethren to repent, enter at the strait gate, continue in the narrow way until eternal life, and be wise.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob urges repentance and continuation in the narrow way until eternal life.
Jacob exhorts his hearers to be wise.

unspecified_visual_details: The audience and setting are not specified.
No literal gate or road is described as visible.

narration.text: repent ye, and enter in at the strait gate,
O be wise; what can I say more?

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The gate and way are figurative teachings.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal gate, road, or travelers.

title: Farewell
summary: Jacob bids farewell and concludes with Amen.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says he will meet those addressed before the pleasing bar of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob is speaking as he concludes his address.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker’s surroundings and the appearance of those addressed are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Finally, I bid you farewell, until I shall meet you before the pleasing bar of God, which bar striketh the wicked with awful dread and fear. Amen.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The meeting before God's bar is described as future, not as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the future meeting or God's bar as a present visible scene.
Do not invent an appearance for God or the people addressed.
